title: Chorus girls, floor shows and comedians
summary: Punch recalls the shows and comedians such as Lollipop Jones.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do they have more shows in Chicago than here, or more here?
Lots of comedians and dancers on the stage and all that.
Yeah, now that's a funny thing, Dick. They used to have a lot of chorus girls and comedians and things here. They ain't got that no more. Here? Right here.
Well these guys used to have practices or have teachers teaching them how to dance and things going here. But they don't have that no more, yeah.
But where did they work? I mean, what clubs?

Well they had, let me see, they had the E-Lights. And then you know, like every time they play a big dance they have a floor show in different halls and they have floor shows and they have girls out there dancing and going on. And the theaters, they was working in the theaters often, see. But they don't have none of that no more. I mean, but one chorus girl, yeah, nah, nah, please tell me she done left. Nah, she gone to Memphis. Her name was May Bell. And what about comedians? Who were some of the comedians? Well, this fellow with Dodge, not some time back. I know his name, Poplar. Yeah. I can't think of him. They got ice cream names, just like him. Is it like Lollipop Jones? Lollipop, Lollipop. Lollipop Jones. Yeah, he's from here.
And he did a lot of clowning and everything in the old days.

Yeah, and this little fellow named Memphis. Memphis. And they had a little, you know, a little guy named Memphis. I heard some people say he wouldn't, but I heard he was from here. He wrote some more. Yeah, he got ice cream names, just like him.
Yeah, he's from here. And he did a lot of clowning and everything in the old days.
